# css-parser

## Project overview
- This repository contains css-parser, a dependency-free all-in-one CSS parsing solution for Node.js and browsers.
- The library follows the CSS Syntax Module Level 3 specification and uses MDN syntax data for validation.
- It is designed for fault-tolerant parsing, full AST and typed-token analysis, AST manipulation, CSS Modules, minification, color processing, and syntax lowering.
- CSS is fully parsed into an arena-backed AST. Nodes and value tokens are integer IDs; their data is accessed through the arena rather than node objects.

## Installation
- npm: npm install @tbela99/css-parser
- jsr: deno add @tbela99/css-parser
- Main entry points:
  - @tbela99/css-parser or @tbela99/css-parser/node
  - @tbela99/css-parser/web

## Core APIs
- parse(css, options): async API; returns {arena, ast, errors, stats}. ast is a stylesheet node ID.
- parseSync(css, options): synchronous equivalent of parse().
- render(arena, ast, options): renders an arena-backed AST and returns a result containing code.
- transform(css, options): async API that parses and renders; returns code with the parse result.
- transformSync(css, options): synchronous equivalent of transform().
- arena.walk(ast, filter): traverses node IDs; filters receive (arena, id).
- parseString(arena, css): parses tokens into the supplied arena.
- parseDeclarations(css, arena?): parses declarations in the supplied arena or a new one; returns {arena, nodes}.
- parse() and transform() also accept input objects for files and readable streams.
- The package is ES module only. Entry points are @tbela99/css-parser, @tbela99/css-parser/node, and @tbela99/css-parser/web.

## Arena-based AST
- Node aliases such as AstRule, AstDeclaration, and Token are numbers, not objects.
- Parse results expose both arena and ast. Use arena methods such as getType(id), getName(id), getSelector(id), getFirstChild(id), and getNextSibling(id) to inspect data.
- Use arena.createRule(), arena.createDeclaration(), arena.createToken(), and related methods to create nodes and tokens.
- arena.toObject(id) returns a live getter/setter view; arena.toPlainObject(id) returns a plain copy.
- AST operations take the arena explicitly: render(arena, ast); use arena.replaceToken(id, ...tokens) to replace a value token.
- Visitors and traversal callbacks receive (arena, id); parent and value data are retrieved through arena methods.
- Detached nodes remain allocated until released or the arena is compacted.
- Transfer an arena between the main thread and a worker with AstArena.toTransferableArenaObject() and AstArena.fromTransferableArenaObjects(). The arena columns are typed-array buffers; this is a zero-copy transfer of node data.

```ts
import {AstArena, parse} from '@tbela99/css-parser';

const {arena, ast} = await parse(css);
const [properties, transferables] = AstArena.toTransferableArenaObject(arena);
worker.postMessage({ast, properties, transferables}, transferables);

// In the worker: reconstruct the arena over the received buffers.
const workerArena = AstArena.fromTransferableArenaObjects(properties, transferables);
```

- Properties such as strings and errors are structured-cloned. Zero-copy transfer of the column buffers detaches the source arena; omit the transfer list to copy the buffers instead.

## Common capabilities
- Parse CSS into an AST and inspect or modify it.
- Validate declarations against CSS syntax definitions.
- Support CSS Modules with scoped class generation.
- Minify CSS safely with options such as inlineCssVariables, computeCalcExpression, removeDuplicateDeclarations, and beautify.
- Transform ASTs through arena methods, visitors, and custom traversal logic.
- Support plugin-style extensions through visitors; handlers receive (arena, id) and inspect or mutate nodes through the arena or an object view.
- Lower modern CSS syntax such as nested CSS and if() to broadly compatible output.
- Generate source maps and handle advanced color functions and conversions.

## Visitor-based plugin model
- The parser exposes a visitor option that accepts node-specific handlers keyed by AST node type and event type.
- Plugins can be implemented as reusable visitor maps that inspect or transform nodes such as Rule, AtRule, Declaration, KeyframesRule, and Value nodes.
- This allows extension code to run alongside the core parser without modifying the parser itself.

## Typical usage
```ts
import {parse, render} from '@tbela99/css-parser';

const css = `.foo { color: red; }`;
const {arena, ast, errors, stats} = await parse(css);
const rule = arena.getFirstChild(ast);

console.log(arena.getSelector(rule));
console.log(render(arena, ast).code);
console.log(errors, stats);
```

For one-step parsing and output generation, use `transform()` or `transformSync()` and read `result.code`.

## Important behavior notes
- parse(), parseSync(), transform() and transformSync() are lenient by default and preserve unknown constructs unless configured otherwise.
- Comments are removed by default; preserve them with removeComments: false or preserveLicense: true.
- Validation errors are available through the parse/transform result and through arena.getState(id) and arena.getErrors(id).
- The library prioritizes compact output while preserving semantics.

## Useful concepts
- parse(), parseSync() return {arena, ast, errors, stats}; ast is an ID in the returned arena.
- render(arena, ast) turns an arena-backed AST into CSS text.
- transform(), transformSync() perform parsing and rendering together and return code.
- AST node IDs can represent StyleSheet, Rule, AtRule, Declaration, Comment, and Keyframes nodes.

## Repository layout
- src/: parser implementation and core library code
- test/: regression and behavior tests
- files/: documentation content used by the docs site
- benchmark/: performance and minification benchmarks
- scripts/: helper scripts and patches
